title: Hello, C++!
description: Print Hello, C++! followed by a newline. This program has no input. Print no additional text.
hints: Use std::cout with a string literal.
Put \n inside the quotes to end the line.

title: Age in Months
description: Read a whole-number age from 0 to 120. Print the age in months, using 12 months per year.
hints: Read into an initialized int.
Multiply by 12.
concepts: Choose int, double, char, and bool

title: Sum of Two Numbers
description: Read two integers, each between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000. Print their sum. Input values may be separated by spaces or newlines.
hints: Use std::cin >> a >> b.
Print a + b; do not print an input prompt.

title: Sum the Even Numbers
description: Read n, with 0 ≤ n ≤ 1000. Print the sum of all even integers from 1 through n, inclusive.
hints: Start an accumulator at zero.
Either test i % 2 == 0, or advance by two.

title: A Square Function
description: Read an integer n between -1000 and 1000. Define a function that calculates its square, call it from main, and print the result.
hints: Place the function above main.
Return n * n, then print the returned value.

title: Return the Maximum
description: Read three integers between -1000 and 1000. Write a function that returns the greatest value, then print that value. Equal inputs are allowed.
hints: Consider the case where the maximum appears first.
Every path through the function must return.

title: Swap by Reference
description: Read two integers. Use a function with two reference parameters to swap them. Print the resulting first and second values separated by one space.
hints: The parameters need & to change the original objects.
Keep the first value in a temporary before overwriting it.
concepts: Modify a caller through a reference

title: Factorial, Carefully
description: Read n, with 0 ≤ n ≤ 20. Write a function to compute n factorial and print it. Define 0 factorial as 1. Use long long for the result.
hints: The multiplication identity is 1, not 0.
20! fits in signed long long but not int.
concepts: Test an operation at its boundaries

title: Count the Vowels
description: Read one line of ASCII text, possibly empty. Count English vowels (a, e, i, o, u) in either uppercase or lowercase and print the count.
hints: Read with getline so spaces are preserved.
A string containing all ten vowel forms can help with membership checks.

title: Sequence Bounds
description: Read n (1–100), followed by n integers between -1000 and 1000. Store them in a vector and print the smallest and largest values, separated by a space.
hints: The input guarantees at least one element.
Initialize both bounds from the first element, not from zero.

title: Distinct Values
description: Read n (0–100), followed by n integers. Insert the values into a set and print the number of distinct values.
hints: A set keeps only one copy of each value.
The answer is the final set size.

title: Put Values in Order
description: Read n (0–100), then n integers. Sort them in ascending order and print them separated by spaces. For n = 0, print an empty line.
hints: Pass begin() and end() to std::sort.
An empty range is already sorted.

title: A Rectangle Type
description: Read two integers width and height (0–1000). Model a Rectangle with an area member function and print its area.
hints: The member function can directly read the object's width and height.
Declare a read-only member function const.

title: Protect the Balance
description: Read an initial balance and a withdrawal amount (each 0–10000). Implement an Account that withdraws only when funds suffice. Print the remaining balance; an unaffordable withdrawal leaves it unchanged.
hints: Keep balance_ private.
Check the amount before subtracting it.

title: One Shape Interface
description: Read a shape word (square or rectangle), then width and height (0–100). For square, area is width squared; ignore height. For rectangle, area is width times height. Use a shared virtual area interface and print the area.
hints: Create a base interface with a virtual area() const.
Keep the selected object alive while using a base reference.
concepts: Use a virtual destructor in an interface

title: A Basket of Values
description: Read n (0–20), followed by n pairs of a single-word product name and integer price (0–10000). Store Product values in a vector and print the total price.
hints: Each Product can hold a string and an int.
The vector owns the product values.

title: Through an Address
description: Read an integer n (-1000–1000). Point to the variable with an int*, double the value through that pointer, and print the variable.
hints: Take the address with &n.
Use *p to read or modify the pointed-to integer.
concepts: Take an address and dereference safely

title: A Managed Buffer
description: Read n (0–100), then n integers (-1000–1000). Store the values in a vector and print their sum. Avoid raw new and delete.
hints: Create a vector with n elements.
The vector releases its allocation when it leaves scope.
concepts: Avoid manual allocation when a container fits

title: Transfer Ownership
description: Read an integer (-1000–1000). Create a unique_ptr<int> owning it, transfer ownership to another unique_ptr, and print the owned value plus one.
hints: Use std::make_unique<int>(n).
std::move allows the unique_ptr move constructor to transfer ownership.
concepts: Use shared ownership only when required

title: Move a Collection
description: Read n (0–100), then n integers. Move a populated vector into a second vector. Print the second vector's size and sum, separated by a space.
hints: Move only after populating the source vector.
Calculate using the destination, without assuming a particular source size.
concepts: Distinguish a move from a copy

title: Edit a Range
description: Read n (0–100), then n integers (-1000–1000). Double each element in place with a range-based loop and print the resulting sequence separated by spaces.
hints: Use auto& when the loop should change the vector.
Printing a copied int is fine.
concepts: Choose value, reference, or const reference in a loop

title: A Focused Predicate
description: Read n (0–100) and a threshold, followed by n integers. Use std::count_if with a lambda to count values strictly greater than the threshold. Print the count.
hints: Capture threshold by value.
The comparison is strictly greater, so equality does not count.

title: A Generic Minimum
description: Read two integers (-1000–1000). Implement a constexpr function template that returns the smaller of two values of the same type. Print its result for the input.
hints: Use template<typename T> above the function.
Return either a or b using a comparison.

title: A Result That May Be Absent
description: Read two integers a and b (-1000–1000). Return an optional integer quotient from a function. Print undefined if b is zero; otherwise print a / b using C++ integer division.
hints: Return std::nullopt for a zero divisor.
Check the optional before dereferencing.
concepts: Check errors before using a value

title: CLI Calculator
description: Read a, an operator, and b (integers -1000–1000). Print the result for +, -, *, or /. Division truncates toward zero. Print undefined for division by zero and invalid for any other operator. Print no prompts. Each run processes one expression.
hints: Read the operator into a char.
Check the divisor before evaluating division.

title: Number Guessing Game
description: Read secret (1–100), then n (0–20), then n guesses (1–100). The secret is supplied as input so tests are reproducible. For each processed guess print low, high, or correct on its own line. Stop after the correct guess. Finally print attempts N, where N is the number of guesses actually processed. This terminal uses prepared input rather than interactive prompts.
hints: The guess that succeeds still counts as an attempt.
With zero guesses, only the attempts line is printed.

title: Simple Contact Manager
description: Read n (0–50), then n commands. add NAME PHONE stores or replaces a contact. get NAME prints its phone or not found. remove NAME deletes a contact if present and prints nothing. Names and phones are single whitespace-free words; phone numbers must remain strings to preserve leading zeros. State is retained within one run. Print only lookup results.
sampleInput:
5
add Ada 0123
get Ada
get Grace
remove Ada
get Ada

tests.input:
5
add Ada 0123
get Ada
get Grace
remove Ada
get Ada

4
add A 12
add A 34
get A
get B

hints: Keep phone numbers as strings.
find avoids inserting a missing contact during lookup.

title: Text Statistics Tool
description: Read ASCII text until EOF. A word is a maximal sequence of non-whitespace characters; punctuation belongs to the word. Count letters A–Z and a–z only. Print three lines: words N, letters N, longest N. longest is the length of the longest word including punctuation. Empty input gives all zeros.
hints: operator>> reads words and naturally skips whitespace.
Count letters separately from the word length.
